To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the κB-binding activity in the adult brain is mainly composed of the p50/c- Rel heterodimer and the BETA factor.

NF-κB-like proteins in the mouse and the rat brain show a developmentally regulated expression and a tissue-specific distribution, and that the major NF-κB-related factor in the adult brain is a heterodimere composed of p50 and Rel.
the expression of κB-binding factors in the mouse brain is developmentally regulated and shows tissue-specificity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the NF-κB-like proteins in the brain and their expression pattern.
the characterization of NF-κB-like proteins in the brain and their expression in the developing mouse and rat.
the characterization and regulation of the transcription factors of the NF-κB family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
κB-like factors in adult brain consist of NF-κB (p50/p65 and p50/c-rel) and BETA (factor A).
the expression of κB-specific factors in the brain is tissue-specific and developmentally regulated.
the brain expresses all κB-binding factors observed so far in other tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the adult mouse and adult rat brain, only NF-κB, p50/c- Rel heterodimer and BETA were observed.
NF-κB is expressed in the brain, but not exclusively, and that it is probably not involved in the regulation of plasticity-related genes.
NF-κB-like activities in the brain are expressed in a developmentally regulated and, in the adult, tissue-specific manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a very complex array of NF-kappa B-like factors in the brain.
the NF-κB family is expressed in the mouse and the rat brain in a developmentally regulated and in a tissue-specific fashion.
the expression of κB-binding activity in the mouse brain is tissue-specific and developmentally regulated.
